title: SOMEONE IS WATCHING ME (FULL TEXT STORY)

format.aspect: 4:5 portrait-ish (downloaded 360x450 @30fps; YouTube long-form, not a Short)
format.medium: fake iOS iMessage screen recording (text story), no voice-over
format.audio: No speech (faster-whisper small: 0 segments; no subs). Ambient horror drone/music bed at about -25 dB that swells at each escalation (120-210 s, 345-435 s, 650-735 s peaks near -11 dB RMS), 0.1 s keyboard-tap clicks while the POV types, send/receive pop SFX per bubble, a lock-screen chime at 0 s, and a quiet bed (-37 dB) under the epilogue text cards.

devices: all caps, 4-word first-person sentence: 'someone is watching me' puts the viewer in the victim's seat
vague antagonist ('someone') = open loop: who and where
present progressive ('is watching') implies it is happening right now
parenthetical format tag '(FULL TEXT STORY)' tells the audience the genre and that this is the long cut of a story likely teased as a Short
title also is the description's first line; tags stack 'scary text story' variants for search
title_pattern.notes: Channel median is 1.5k; this hit 11k (7.5x). The topic (stranger texting a girl alone at night, sends a photo of her taken through the window) is the most universal home-alone fear; the title is pure premise with no twist spoiled.

thumbnail.composition: 16:9. A single giant iOS notification banner (white, rounded corners) spans ~95% width across the middle third; small green Messages icon + grey 'MESSAGES' label, then 'Unknown Number' bold and the message line. Background: dark, desaturated blood-red wall with vertical drips/streaks, vignette at edges. Top-right: 'FULL VIDEO' in thick white hand-brush caps.
thumbnail.text: 'Unknown Number' / 'I'M WATCHING YOU' (system font, black, large), 'FULL VIDEO' (white brush font, top right). Note: 'I'M WATCHING YOU' never appears in the video; it is a paraphrased hook line.
thumbnail.colours: Clean white card + black SF-style text vs muddy dark red/maroon dripping background; one green icon accent. Very high luminance contrast in the centre.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: No person or face. The 'subject' is the phone notification blown up to billboard size; the scale exaggeration of a familiar small UI element is the contrast. Cosy everyday UI vs gore-coded blood-drip wall.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Instantly legible at any size (three lines of text), mimics a real lock-screen notification so it triggers the 'someone texted me' reflex, the message is a direct second-person threat that implicates the viewer, and the blood-drip backdrop signals horror without showing anything. 'FULL VIDEO' converts viewers who saw the Short/TikTok part 1.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [lock screen, 10:11, Saturday, November 29 - notification] Unknown Number: What's your favorite scary movie? -> [chat opens] Unknown Number: What's your favorite scary movie? / Me: Huh?
hook.verbatim_0_12s: Unknown: What's your favorite scary movie? / Me: Huh? / Me: Who is this? / Unknown: Tell me / Unknown: I want to know
hook.device: Cold open on a late-night lock-screen notification from an 'Unknown Number' (B&W close-up of a girl's face as wallpaper = the victim), with a Scream-style creepy opener question. Zero setup, zero exposition: the viewer reads the first message within 1 s. The stranger refuses to identify himself and repeats the question (insistence = menace). Silent-reading format, so the hook is read, not heard; the open loop is 'who is this and why do they care'.

beats.summary: Lock screen 10:11 PM, Saturday; Unknown Number asks 'What's your favorite scary movie?'
POV asks who this is; stranger only repeats 'tell me / I want to know' and the question; she says wrong number.
Stranger apologises ('my bad, wrong number'), then pivots: 'or maybe life just wants us to talk', random connections. POV: 'Umm... okay?'
He circles back to the same question for the third time, 'it says a lot about a person'; she gives in: The Conjuring.
He describes the clapping-in-the-dark-hallway scene, 'my heart races'; the referenced scene (someone unseen inside the house) foreshadows the ending.
'Can we be friends? ... to know who you really are'; name trade; she gives her real name, Sophia.
'I love that name' ... 'I also love your pink dress Sophia' - 'My what?' - he sends a dark photo of her in a pink top taken from outside. Midpoint shock at 25% of runtime.
All-caps burst: WHAT?? WHERE ARE YOU? ARE YOU WATCHING ME? TELL ME WHERE YOU ARE. WHO IS THIS? No reply (silence as threat).
Black 'FEW MINUTES LATER' card, lock screen 10:20 with a notification from Lisa; switch to the best-friend chat.
Sophia recaps for Lisa (recap doubles as a re-hook for viewers arriving late) and clarifies the photo was taken right now, from the window.
Lisa: close curtains, lock all doors; asks if she is alone - mom? brother? anyone? Stranger interrupts with a 'Don't be scared' banner (he knows what is being said).
Sophia is home alone; family went out. Lisa: call the police; Sophia already did, officers on their way. Lisa: stay calm and hidden.
Notification banners over the chat: 'Which do you think is more deadly?' / 'A knife or a gun'. Sophia: he keeps messaging nonstop.
Incoming call banner from Unknown Number; Lisa: block him; Sophia already did - somehow he can still text and call. 'How is that even possible?'
Lisa's rapid list of rules: don't panic, ignore, don't respond, don't answer, don't look outside, wait for police, he's probably just a loser.
'OH MY GOD' -> Lisa caps panic -> the power just went out; only her house is dark (neighbours and streetlight on); 'what if he tampered with my electricity?'
Police timing uncertain, 'I'm getting scared, Lisa'; Lisa: doors are locked, he can't get in.
'LISA' -> 'I just heard something, from downstairs' -> someone is in the house; she's in her locked bedroom; Lisa: do not open the door no matter what.
Footsteps, on the stairs, coming upstairs, getting closer, OH NO; Lisa: what happened? say something (silence beat).
HE'S AT THE DOOR / BANGING / TRYING TO BREAK IT DOWN / THE DOOR IS BREAKING / IT'S OPENING; Lisa: WHAT? RUN. RUN SOPHIA. Chat ends.

Black screen, serif white typewriter text: he broke the door, she fought, he killed her with the knife in his left hand (pays off 'knife or a gun'); police found her body and broken phone; killer never found.
'The end.'

pacing.avg_shot_length_s: ~110 s between true cuts (lock screen, time card, lock screen, chat switch, black, cards); but a new bubble lands every ~3.5 s and typed-out outgoing text animates every few seconds, so effective visual change interval is ~2-3.5 s
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~40-60 s: each re-hook is a new threat (photo 198 s, banner 354 s, knife-or-gun 406 s, call 444 s, block fails 480 s, power cut 528 s, noise downstairs 632 s, footsteps 682 s, door 722 s)
pacing.in_story_clock: Phone clock runs 10:11 -> 10:15 in chat 1 and 10:20 -> 10:28 in chat 2, and battery drains 82% -> 73%: the video is roughly real-time, which sells authenticity

transcript_source: No speech and no YouTube subs; on-screen text read visually from frames sampled every 2 s (research/library/transcripts/Xv32FAAUI-0.txt, timestamps = first appearance +-2 s).
techniques_worth_copying: Lock-screen notification cold open: the first frame is the hook text itself, readable in under 1 s, with the time (late night) and 'Unknown Number' doing the setting.
Antagonist repeats the same innocent question three times; repetition turns a harmless line into menace without any gore.
False relief beat ('my bad, wrong number') right before the pivot ('or maybe life wants us to talk') - a fake exit that tightens the hook at ~45 s.
Foreshadow via a pop-culture scene the villain describes (unseen presence inside the house) that the ending then re-enacts; write our own equivalent, not this one.
The 'he can see you' reveal uses a specific detail (the pink dress) and then a photo; the detail lands before the image, so the reader's dread arrives a beat early.
Switch from the stranger thread to a best-friend thread after the midpoint; the recap to the friend re-hooks late arrivals and the friend becomes the voice of false reassurance.
Villain intrudes on the friend chat via OS notification banners and an incoming-call banner - uses the phone UI itself as the jump scare, no extra assets needed.
Rule-break escalation: blocked number can still text and call - signals the threat is beyond normal rules.
Escalation ladder of physical proximity: outside window -> power cut (only her house) -> noise downstairs -> footsteps -> stairs -> door -> opening.
One idea per bubble, 2-6 words, stacked rapidly; caps bubbles reserved for panic peaks (27 of 222).
Silence as a beat: the stranger never answers WHO IS THIS?, and Sophia goes silent while Lisa asks 'say something' before the climax.
Ending: chat cuts mid-crisis on the friend's 'RUN SOPHIA', then a typewriter epilogue in serif on black gives a definitive bleak outcome and pays off an earlier line (knife vs gun).
Realism details: in-phone clock and battery progress through the video, 'Delivered' receipts, outgoing text typed letter by letter with keyboard clicks.
Packaging: thumbnail is a giant notification with a second-person threat line on a blood-drip wall; title is a first-person present-tense statement plus a '(FULL TEXT STORY)' format tag.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Very high - this is the most code-friendly horror format. Everything except the one photo is UI rendering: a React iMessage clone in Remotion driven by a JSON script of {t, sender, text} plus event entries (banner, call, card, lockscreen). The one photo must be replaced by an SVG/canvas 'grainy night photo through a window' illustration or a stylised silhouette (no AI imagery, no stock person).
components: PhoneFrame/StatusBar: carrier dots, wifi, clock that advances with story time, battery % that drains
ThreadHeader: letter avatar circle + name, back chevron, phone/info icons, optional blurred glow
Bubble: incoming grey (#E5E5EA, black text) and outgoing blue (#0B84FF/#1A8CFF, white text), tail on last bubble of a group, max width ~70%, 'Delivered' receipt under the latest outgoing
Auto-scroll layout: measure bubble heights, keep the newest bubble anchored above the input bar, spring scroll on each insert
InputBar: camera/app icons, pill text field with caret; outgoing messages type in character by character (~12-18 chars/s) before the send pop
TypingIndicator (three-dot or ghost text) before incoming messages
NotificationBanner: white rounded card with Messages icon, sender, text, slide down from top, 2-6 s hold
IncomingCallBanner: dark translucent pill, avatar, name, 'mobile', red/green round buttons
LockScreen: big thin clock + date, 'Earlier Today', notification card, generic wallpaper (draw an abstract or SVG face/silhouette, not a real photo)
TitleCard: black + condensed caps ('A FEW MINUTES LATER')
TypewriterCard: serif white text on black, per-character reveal, paragraph swap
code_only_remake_needs.fonts: SF Pro is Apple-licensed: use Inter or a similar system-like sans for bubbles, Bebas Neue for time cards, a book serif (e.g. Lora/Libre Baskerville) for the epilogue. Avoid exact Apple trademarks/UI chrome where it matters; a near-iMessage style is enough.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Royalty-free or self-generated ambient drone that swells per act, a soft pop for receive, whoosh for send, keyboard tick per typed character, a chime for the lock-screen notification, a ringtone loop during the call banner. All can be synthesized (WebAudio/sox) or CC0.
code_only_remake_needs.timing_engine: Script compiler converting messages to frames: incoming bubble every ~2-4 s, outgoing = typing time (chars/15 s) + 0.3 s, caps bursts at ~1.5-2 s, epilogue typed at ~25 chars/s; target ~70 on-screen words/min, ~220 messages per 13 min.
code_only_remake_needs.format_variants: Long-form 4:5 or 9:16 canvas (1080x1350 / 1080x1920), and a 60 s Short cut ending on the midpoint photo reveal as the teaser for the 'FULL VIDEO'.
code_only_remake_needs.thumbnail: SVG: blood-drip/grunge red background (procedural noise + vertical drip paths), oversized white notification card with a second-person threat line, 'FULL VIDEO' brush-caps tag.
